Adverse childhood experiences and adult health (simulated)

ace_study.Rd

2,500 adults with eight binary adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), three confounders and two adult health outcomes. Designed for intervene_effect(): hypothetical interventions that prevent some ACEs (e.g. abuse and neglect, ace1 and ace2). Because the data are simulated, the true effects are known (see Source).

Usage

ace_study

Format

A data frame with 2,500 rows and 14 columns:

id

Respondent id.

ace1

Abuse (emotional or physical) before age 18 (0/1).

ace2

Neglect (emotional or physical) (0/1).

ace3

Sexual abuse (0/1).

ace4

Witnessed domestic violence (0/1).

ace5

Household substance misuse (0/1).

ace6

Household mental illness (0/1).

ace7

Parental separation or divorce (0/1).

ace8

Incarcerated household member (0/1).

age

Age in years, 25–64 (confounder).

female

1 = woman (confounder).

parent_edu

Parents' years of education, 6–20 (confounder).

health

Self-rated health today, 0–100 (EQ VAS style; 100 = best imaginable).

depressed

Depressed in the past year (0/1).

No values are missing.

Source

Simulated by datasets/generate.jl of LatentClassCausal.jl (seed Xoshiro(20261112)); codebook in its datasets/README.md. A three-class latent family context (Low adversity, Household dysfunction, Maltreatment), more adverse with lower parental education, generates the eight ACEs (prevalences .19, .14, .08, .20, .23, .20, .29, .08). The outcomes depend on ace1, ace2 (with an interaction), ace6 and the confounders but not on the latent context directly, so the effects of intervening on ace1 and ace2 are identified given the other ACEs and the confounders: E(health) = 80 - 6 ace1 - 5 ace2 - 3 ace1 ace2 - 2.5 ace6 - 0.2 (age - 45) - 1.5 female + 0.6 (parent_edu - 12), residual SD 12; logit P(depressed) = -2.3

  • 0.7 ace1 + 0.6 ace2 + 0.3 ace1 ace2 + 0.4 ace6 - 0.01 (age - 45) + 0.5 female - 0.06 (parent_edu - 12). True effects against the natural course (health 76.78, depressed 0.167): preventing both, setto(c(0, 0)), psi = +2.00 (health) and -0.038 (depressed); halving both, shift(0.5), psi = +1.04 and -0.021. Licence: CC0 1.0 (public domain).

Raw survey files often code missing values as -999; convert them first (dat[dat == -999] <- NA) and decide on complete cases or imputation: the estimators need complete data.

Examples

data(ace_study)
# prevalence of each ACE and mean self-rated health with and without abuse (ace1)
round(colMeans(ace_study[, paste0("ace", 1:8)]), 3)
#>  ace1  ace2  ace3  ace4  ace5  ace6  ace7  ace8 
#> 0.186 0.142 0.077 0.197 0.234 0.196 0.291 0.081 
tapply(ace_study$health, ace_study$ace1, mean)
#>        0        1 
#> 78.41798 69.16810 
# \donttest{
# would preventing childhood abuse and neglect (ace1, ace2) improve adult health?
intervene_effect(ace_study, outcome = health, exposures = ace1:ace8,
                    intervene = c(ace1, ace2), confounders = c(age, female, parent_edu),
                    g1 = setto(c(0, 0)))
#> Starting Julia ...
#> ▸ Effect of a hypothetical intervention on exposures
#>   AIPW, 5-fold cross-fitting, gaussian outcome; N = 2500
#>   Outcome:      health
#>   Intervene:    ace1, ace2
#>   Adjusted for: ace3, ace4, ace5, ace6, ace7, ace8, age, female, parent_edu
#>   g1:           set to (0, 0)
#>   g0:           natural course
#> 
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>                        Estimate     SE            95% CI      p
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   E[Yᵍ¹]                 78.965  0.305  [78.367, 79.563]       
#>   E[Yᵍ⁰]                 76.701  0.255  [76.202, 77.201]       
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   ψ = E[Yᵍ¹] − E[Yᵍ⁰]     2.264  0.208    [1.855, 2.673]  <.001
#>   ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#>   Overlap: min P(A_S = s | H) = 0.0050, max weight = 10.1
#>   ⚠ near-violation of positivity: some post-intervention profiles are rare
# true psi = +2.00 points on the 0-100 scale
# }
